title: Travel Vocabulary
description: Learn important words for airports, hotels, and traveling.

thumbnail.alt: A suitcase and a passport on a table

back.definition: The bags and suitcases you take on a trip.
back.example: Where can I pick up my luggage?

back.definition: An official document you need to travel to another country.
back.example: Please show your passport at the desk.

back.definition: A piece of paper or electronic document that shows you paid for a journey.
back.example: I bought a train ticket to London.

image.alt: A person working on an airplane, serving drinks

back.definition: A person who serves and takes care of passengers on an aircraft.
back.example: The flight attendant brought me some water.

image.alt: A large building with many windows and a reception desk

back.definition: A place where you pay to sleep when you are traveling.
back.example: We booked a room in a nice hotel near the beach.

image.alt: A person pointing at a famous building, talking to a group

back.definition: A person whose job is to show tourists around a place of interest.
back.example: Our tour guide knew everything about the history of the city.

image.alt: A small object bought as a memory, like a magnet or a mug

back.definition: Something you buy or keep to remember a place you visited.
back.example: I bought a magnet as a souvenir from Paris.

image.alt: A desk at an airport where officials check bags

back.definition: The place at a port or airport where officials check what you are bringing into a country.
back.example: It took an hour to go through customs.

image.alt: A calendar and a phone booking a date

back.definition: An arrangement to have a room or seat saved for you.
back.example: I have a reservation for two nights.

image.alt: An airport sign showing planes taking off

back.definition: The act of leaving a place, especially when starting a journey.
back.example: Check the screen for our flight's departure time.
